title: Prospective Reserve Allocator and Oscillation Mitigator — PRD (draft)
content:
Summary:
This doc proposes the Prospective Reserve Allocator (PRA): a predictive, short-duration reservation and smoothing controller for Dedicated capacity that reduces oscillation (hot-cold churn), improves fairness for unpredictable workloads, and provides explicit isolation windows for high-priority routes. PRA is targeted at customers on Dedicated who have bursty traffic patterns that cause frequent scale/evict cycles for other customers on the same physical pool.

Problem space and motivating examples:
- Our current Dedicated reservation and prewarm heuristics handle steady growth well but struggle with rapidly shifting demand from short-lived campaigns (ad pushes, feature launches, data migrations). The result: repeated autoscaler churn, degraded latency tail for mid-tier customers, and noisy neighbor complaints.
- Example A: Customer X ramps for 7–12 minutes with 10× request rate, then drops to baseline. The autoscaler spins up new slots, other tenants get preempted repeatedly.
- Example B: Customer Y has an unpredictable afternoon traffic spike each week; current smoothing parameters either over-provision for long periods or cause repeated evictions.

Design goals (what success looks like):
1) Reduce autoscaler oscillation metric by >= 35% for affected pools (measured by number of scale events per hour per pool).
2) Ensure 99th percentile latency for dedicated tenants remains within SLO during short spikes (target: < 1.3× baseline 99p).
3) Provide an opt-in per-route isolation window mechanism so customers can buy or request short reservation windows with strict isolation guarantees.
4) Keep additional cost/idle capacity overhead under 8% on average across typical pools.
5) Transparent observability: customers and ops can see PRA decisions, prediction confidence, and fallback actions in Console.

Core concepts / terminology:
- Prospective Reserve (PR): a short-duration, tentatively allocated capacity slice backed by predictive signal. Not a hard reservation until confirmed.
- Momentum Token: a bookkeeping unit that encodes recent upward velocity for a route's demand. Consumed when PR is granted and decays over time.
- Isolation Window: a flagged PR that elevates enforcement (hard isolation) for a limited duration. Requires entitlement or explicit customer opt-in.
- Oscillation Mitigator: adaptive decay and hold-back logic in the controller to avoid repeatedly allocating and deallocating the same physical resources.

How PRA differs from existing approaches:
- Prediction-first: leverages short-horizon demand forecasts (30s–10m) plus velocity to create PRs rather than only reacting to queue depth or token consumption.
- Soft-confirmation path: if prediction confidence is low, PRA issues a tentative PR (soft) that uses opportunistic spillover capacity; only converts to hard PR when sustained signal observed.
- Momentum-based smoothing: favors keeping a small buffer for routes exhibiting positive momentum instead of immediate decommit on first downsample.

User stories / endpoints:
- As an SRE I want to see PRA forecast and decision traces for any scale action so I can audit why a route gained a PR.
- As a product engineer I want to opt my analytics route into a 5-minute Isolation Window for a launch so we don’t get preempted.
- As an ops engineer I want PRA to preemptively throttle probabilistic low-priority work instead of evicting living tenants during a pool squeeze.

Controller behavior (high-level):
1) Signal ingestion: per-route request rates, recent schedule hints, business-calendar tags (e.g., marketing push), and historic daily patterns.
2) Forecasting: a lightweight ensemble (exponential smoothing + short-window linear regressor) produces a 30s, 2m, and 10m horizon forecast with confidence score.
3) Decision layer: when forecast exceeds a route's effective headroom threshold we create a PR with parameters: duration, isolation_level (none | soft | hard), momentum_tokens_required, and spill_policy.
4) Execution: PRs map to either: a) soft assignment (use spare capacity if available, can be preempted), b) shadow-deploy (cold standby slot warmed to reduced readiness), or c) hard isolation (strict capacity carved out; paid or entitlement required).
5) Holdback & decay: after the spike, PRs are retained for a configurable decay window based on momentum tokens rather than immediate decommit.

Configuration & API (sketch):
- PRA policy config (per-customer or per-route):
  - forecast_horizon_seconds: string (e.g., "600")
  - min_isolation_duration_seconds: string
  - max_soft_pr_percentage: string (percent of pool allocatable to soft PRs)
  - momentum_decay_seconds: string
  - priority_score: string (0-100)
- Admin API endpoints:
  - POST /pra/policies/: create/update policy (accepts JSON body)
  - GET /pra/traces?route=: returns prediction & decision trace (used by Console)
  - POST /pra/isolation-requests: request a hard isolation window (requires approval or billing entitlement)

Observability & Console UX notes:
- New PRA tab under Dedicated pool view: shows active PRs, their type (soft/hard), confidence, predicted peak, and momentum tokens.
- Timeline view: compact trace of forecasts vs actuals and any convert-to-hard events.
- Alerts: ops receives an alert when PR conversion rate or false-positive rate exceeds thresholds.

Operational flow & runbook (ops-focused):
- Normal operation: PRA runs autonomously with conservative defaults.
- When pool pressure rises: PRA reduces soft PR acceptance and favors momentum reduction; sends advisory to pool SREs.
- When lagging forecasts produce repeated false positives: throttling back the predictor (increase confidence threshold) and runbook step to inspect training features.
- Emergency override: ops can pause PRA for a pool and forcibly reconcile capacity using existing autoscaler semantics.

Rollout plan (phases):
- Phase 0 (lab): validation against historical traces (2–4 weeks). Metric: false-conversion < 20%.
- Phase 1 (canary): enable PRA in 1–2 non-critical pools with soft-PR only for 2 weeks. Monitor scale event rate, 99p latency, and cost delta.
- Phase 2 (wider beta): expand to more pools; introduce shadow-deploy option (partial warm).
- Phase 3 (GA): add hard isolation request flow and Console UI; open to customers with entitlement.

Success metrics / KPIs:
- Autoscaler events per pool/hour (target: -35% in pilot pools).
- Conversion fidelity: fraction of PRs that convert to hard-confirmed allocation (target 60–80% depending on policy).
- Cost overhead: average extra idle allocation caused by PRA (target < 8%).
- Customer isolation requests processed and satisfaction score from CS pilot customers.

Risks and open questions:
- Prediction quality: forecasts may be poor for new routes with no history — need synthetic priors and conservative fallbacks.
- Economic model: how to bill for Isolation Windows vs soft PRs; whether to surface costs in Console in real-time.
- Complex interactions with existing autoscaler rules; need reconciliation policy to avoid double-counting.
- Security/abuse: a customer could repeatedly request short isolation windows to game priority; need throttles and approval.

Implementation notes / engineering tasks (rough):
- infra: add PRA decision service + compact time-series store for short-horizon features. (ENG-PR-1)
- serving-runtime: API hooks to allocate soft vs hard capacity and to honor momentum tokens in eviction logic. (ENG-PR-2)
- console: new PRA panel and traces endpoint. (ENG-PR-3)
- billing: add isolation-window SKU and metering. (ENG-PR-4)
- metrics: autoscaler_event_count, pra_pr_created, pra_pr_converted, pra_false_positive_rate. (ENG-PR-5)

Notes to reviewers / TODOs:
- Need feedback from SRE (Jonah) on fail-open semantics for pool pressure scenarios.
- Confirm acceptable billing model alternatives with finance & sales (Priya).
- Validate predictor features with Applied ML (Ethan) — flags: calendar-based hints, external webhooks.
- Add example API payloads and a minimal schema in a follow-up doc.

Appendix — quick sketch of momentum token mechanics:
- Each route accrues momentum_tokens on upward rate changes: tokens = floor(delta_rate / token_unit).
- Tokens decay exponentially with half-life = momentum_decay_seconds.
- A PR requires N tokens to convert from soft to hard; if conversion doesn't happen before duration expires, tokens partially refunded (to avoid permanent credit accrual).

Quick open questions I want input on:
- Should soft PRs be visible to customers (yes if we show expected cost/operational impact) or hidden?
- Minimal isolation SLAs for hard isolation (SLA: 99.9% availability during window?).
- Charge model: flat per-minute for isolation windows or usage-based uplift?

References / links (placeholders):
- JIRA RDW-3214 — PRA forecasting service spike analysis
- Confluence: prospective-reserve-allocator (proto and notes)
- GitHub PR: prospective-reserve-adapter-PR-78

End.
